questions.question: Which dated event controls a Texas governmental entity's Chapter 2251 payment clock, and when does the ordinary or monthly-meeting political-subdivision period become overdue?
questions.scope: Contract for goods or services with a Texas state agency or political subdivision; excludes legal advice on remedies and separate public-work bond claims.
questions.answer: Section 2251.021(a) uses the later of goods receipt, completed service or invoice receipt. For example, if goods arrive March 1, service completes March 10 and the invoice is received March 20, March 20 is the trigger; the ordinary payment becomes overdue on the 31st day after that date (the state payment guide describes payment as due by day 30). A qualifying political subdivision whose governing body meets once a month or less uses the 46th day under §2251.021(b). The legal-services state-agency exception in §2251.021(b-1) is a separate 46-day rule.

questions.question: How should a disputed Texas governmental invoice and downstream subcontractor payment be controlled?
questions.scope: Texas governmental-entity vendor/subcontractor payment chain under Chapter 2251; dispute notice and statutory timing only.
questions.answer: Under §2251.042(a), the governmental entity must notify the vendor of an invoice error or disputed amount no later than the 21st day after invoice receipt and give a detailed statement of the disputed amount. If resolved for the vendor, interest on the unpaid balance starts from the §2251.021 overdue date; if resolved for the entity, the vendor submits a corrected invoice subject to that section. Separately, a vendor receiving the governmental payment must pay the subcontractor's appropriate share by the 10th day after receipt under §2251.022(a), with day 11 overdue. The ledger should therefore preserve governmental receipt, dispute notice, resolution, corrected invoice and downstream receipt dates separately.
